children: , the cloud, productivity and cybersecurity company, disrupted the EvilTokens cybercrime service through a court-authorized operation with law enforcement and industry partners. Shares were quoted at $497.64 in the September 23 chart. The chart does not show a daily percentage move, so the earlier 1.1% gain cannot be carried over to this price.

Microsoft says the operation seized 50 websites and disabled more than 150 related domains. According to Axios, EvilTokens compromised more than 12,000 inboxes across 10,000 organizations. Its operators used AI to sift through stolen email for payment conversations and people worth impersonating. One stolen account could become a map for the next fraud attempt.

The chart puts Microsoft's $497.64 share price 15.2% below its $586.84 GF Value estimate. That gap is a valuation signal, not proof the stock is cheap. For Microsoft 365, the bigger test is whether stronger account protection can stop attackers before they turn a trusted inbox into a fraud tool. The takedown removed infrastructure; preventing the next compromise is what customers will feel.

title: Microsoft Stays Flat After Cutting an AI Phishing Supply Chain
